summary: This Docker Compose file sets up a Joomla website with a MySQL database, both running in containers on the same network. It uses environment variables with default fallback values so you can customize the setup without editing the file directly—just pass different values when you start it up.

explanations.1: The ${PROJECT_NAME:-your-project-name} syntax means 'use the PROJECT_NAME environment variable, but if it's not set, default to your-project-name'.
explanations.5: Similarly, this pulls the Joomla version from an environment variable, defaulting to 'latest' if you don't specify one.
explanations.9: This maps port 8080 on your computer to port 80 inside the container, so you'll visit localhost:8080 in your browser to access Joomla.
explanations.25: This tells Docker that the Joomla service shouldn't start until the joomladb service is healthy (meaning the database is actually ready to accept connections).
explanations.28: This runs the container as a specific user ID and group ID instead of root, which is a security best practice.
explanations.39: There's a typo here—it should be ${MYSQL_PORT:-3306} without the dash before the colon; as written it won't properly default to 3306.
explanations.43: Setting this to '1' tells MySQL to generate a random root password automatically instead of using a fixed one.
explanations.46: This health check periodically runs a command inside the container to verify MySQL is running; Docker uses this to know when the database is actually ready.
